title: Preview for Zombie Survival ARPG - And a bit on how I built it
author: Semantic_meaning
selftext:
It's a browser ARPG in three.js where you survive waves of the dead with a pistol that you can deeply customize with a 250 node skill tree. I just broke ground on development so it's shallow but I feel like enough is here to capture some of the potential. 

The plan is to expand this into a fully open world zombie survival game, and the systems are now in a place where I can take it there. Every key system in the game is owned by what's called a workbench, an open source standard that I'm building. A workbench is one job, packaged: the model, the skills, the tools, the runtime, and the checks required to verify the outcome. Game systems have one. Mobs have one. Items have one. Biome...etc. (Need to build a UI one). 

That lets each job use a different setup. Opus 5.5 of works well for most things but it's overkill and expensive for many tasks. GPT 6.1 Terra, with a different set of skills and Blender, worked just as well for characters. Each workbench runs in its own sandbox, so I could keep many sessions going in parallel. One night of runs made 12 mob concepts for about $9.80. Then I merged the work back in with Opus in CC.

Anyways, this is the first game I've ever built and this is mainly a showcase of how to build with workbenches, but figured there were some more people out there into the idea of zombie survival  ARPG hybrid. 

play it here : [https://dead-acre.fly.dev](https://dead-acre.fly.dev)
